parts.text: In this experiment, you will determine the resistance per unit length of a resistance wire. The circuit has been set up for you. Carry out the following instructions, referring to Fig. 3.1. Fig. 3.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Connect the crocodile clip to a length l = 20.0 cm of the resistance wire. Close the switch. Measure and record in Table 3.1, the value of potential difference (p.d.) V and current I for the resistance wire. Connect the crocodile clip to lengths l = 40.0 cm, l = 60.0 cm, l = 80.0 cm and l = 100.0 cm of the resistance wire. For each length l , measure and record in Table 3.1, the value of potential difference V and current I for the resistance wire. Open the switch. Table 3.1 l / cm V / V I / A R / Ω 20.0 40.0 60.0 80.0 100.0 [2]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) For each length l calculate and record in Table 3.1, the resistance R of the resistance wire. Use your values of V and I from Table 3.1 and the equation R = V I . [2]

ms.label: 3(b)
ms.text:
correct calculations of R
to consistent 2 or consistent 3 significant figures

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Plot a graph of R / Ω ( y -axis) against l / cm ( x -axis). Draw a straight line of best fit. [4]

ms.label: 3(c)
ms.text:
graph:
•
axes labelled with quantity and unit
•
appropriate scales (plots occupying at least ½ grid)
•
plots all correct to ½ small square and precise plots
•

parts.text: (d) (i) Determine the gradient G of the graph. Show clearly on the graph how you obtained the necessary information. G = ......................................................... [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) The gradient G is numerically equal to the resistance per unit length R 0 of the resistance wire. Write down the value of R 0 for the resistance wire. R 0 = ............................................... Ω / cm [1]
